title: API key shadow reconciliation window causing stale org access during rotation
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary:
A customer escalation reported users in a Dedicated deployment were able to access the previous org scope for a short window after an API key rotation. After investigation we found similar, intermittent reproductions in Hosted and Private deployments under high write/failover load. The issue manifested as short-lived authorization mismatches where requests authenticated with a rotated API key were accepted but evaluated with stale org bindings for up to ~45 seconds in some clusters. This allowed read access to org-scoped resources in that window.

Impact: several customers flagged precision-sensitive data exposures (read-only), leading to escalations and a targeted emergency fix. This ticket tracks the bugfix, rollout, tests, and follow-ups.
steps_taken: 03-05 02:12 UTC - Pager alert from monitoring: surge in 403->200 anomalies for org-scoped routes; customer support escalated
03-05 02:27 UTC - Incident bridge formed; initial triage indicated discrepancy between control-plane key state and edge cache entries
03-05 03:05 UTC - Reproduced locally by simulating rapid apikey rotation + node failover; observed Redis cache TTL and control-plane publish race
03-05 06:10 UTC - Emergency hotfix v1 deployed to edge (reject keys if central version > local version) as a temporary hard-fail to reduce exposure
03-06 09:00 UTC - Scoped patch implemented to introduce tombstone + version stamping on key rotation and immediate pub/sub invalidation to all runtime nodes
03-08 14:00 UTC - Canary rollout across one Dedicated pool and two Hosted regions; no regressions observed in 72h
03-11 21:30 UTC - Full rollout completed to all active clusters (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) with migration script to resync key metadata
root_cause_summary: A race condition between API key rotation propagation and local edge cache reconciliation allowed nodes to accept tokens while still using stale org-scoping metadata. Contributing factors: (1) control-plane publish used eventual pub/sub with no tombstone semantics; (2) local runtime caches accepted last-known-good metadata if central version was not strictly greater; (3) HA failover paths sometimes replayed request authentication using warm caches without forcing a revalidation against control plane during rotations.
mitigation_deployed: Introduced explicit versioned apikey metadata and tombstone markers on rotation, implemented synchronous invalidation pub/sub path for critical key events, and added a short-lived local grace check that forces central verifications if rotation detected. Also added an emergency policy to fail-open->fail-closed depending on customer tier to avoid silent acceptance.
rollout_plan: Canary (1 Dedicated pool, 2 Hosted regions) -> 72h observation -> increment to full fleet over 48h. Private deployments received an upgrade bundle and migration runbook; customers with air-gapped installs were coordinated individually. Post-rollout validation included sampling auth traces and replay tests against known rotated keys.
test_plan: Unit tests for versioned key parsing, integration tests that simulate rotation+failover, chaos tests injecting node restarts during rotation, and e2e replay tests against a sandbox tenant. Added a regression test to CI that replicates the 45s stale window scenario to prevent reintroduction.
monitoring_changes: Added dashboards: 'apikey-rotation-latency', 'authz-stale-window', and a new alert when expired key acceptance rate > 0.1% over 5m. Instrumented metrics for control-plane publish latency and subscriber ack times.
